Reproduction is further hindered by missing code and missing details such as selected DomainNet classes, exact splits, baseline-specific tuning, adapter initialization, preprocessing, and the UCF101 video protocol.

The claimed cross-modal interaction is not demonstrated: the shared matrix is applied separately to each modality, and there is no untied-projection, vision-only/text-only, or representation-alignment ablation. Thus the proposed explanation is stronger than the evidence.

The domain-shift evaluation contains a serious internal inconsistency. Under the described one-client-per-domain protocol, changing the within-domain Dirichlet concentration should be vacuous, and zero-shot CLIP should be invariant. Several headline gains are negligible—for example, 0.02% HM for ViT-B/32 at two shots and 0.05 accuracy points on CIFAR-10 at beta=10—while pFedMMA loses some aggregate and per-dataset settings. The paper appears to select the scaling factor and starting layer using reported base/novel test performance, but specifies no validation protocol. Baseline-specific hyperparameter tuning is also undocumented, with one SGD learning rate apparently applied to every method.
